name: Dallas Love Field
before:
Dallas's city airport, 6 miles north west of downtown, and effectively Southwest Airlines' home. Southwest was born here, has its corporate headquarters here, and held about 95 per cent of the market as of August 2021.

That shapes everything. There are 20 gates in a single terminal and Southwest leases 19 of them. Delta leases the remaining one. JSX operates from its own private terminal on the south side rather than the main building, so a client on JSX should not be sent to the main terminal.

If an itinerary needs a wider choice of airlines, that means Dallas Fort Worth, not Love Field. Love Field was Dallas's main airport until DFW opened in 1974.

Getting in is straightforward. The DART Love Link shuttle connects the terminal to Inwood/Love Field station on the Orange and Green light rail lines, and it is free leaving the terminal.

The airport is named after Moss L. Love, a US Army officer killed in a crash near San Diego.
after:
Dallas's city airport, 6 miles north west of downtown, is effectively Southwest Airlines' home. Southwest was born here and has its headquarters here. US Department of Transportation figures give Southwest about 98 per cent of passengers in the year to June 2026.

That shapes everything. The single terminal has 20 gates, and Southwest and Delta are the only airlines using it. A client flying JSX, a public charter airline, should not be sent there, as JSX uses private terminals.

If an itinerary needs a wider choice of airlines, that means Dallas Fort Worth, not Love Field. Love Field was Dallas's main airport until DFW opened in 1974.

Getting in is straightforward. DART's Love Link bus (route 5) connects the terminal to Inwood/Love Field station on the Orange and Green rail lines.

The airport is named after Moss Lee Love, a US Army officer killed in a crash near San Diego.

claims.inAfter: A client flying JSX, a public charter airline, should not be sent there, as JSX uses private terminals.
claims.note: Was 'JSX operates from its own private terminal on the south side rather than the main building'. JSX's own pages describe a public charter service flying between private facilities and terminals, and the 2006 law lets charter airlines without leased gates use non-terminal facilities at Love Field. The side of the airport is cut: Wikipedia's current article says south in one place and north in another. JSX's readable pages did not name Dallas, so its Love Field service rests on Wikipedia (current article, September 2026); the sentence is written so that it holds for any JSX client. Worth Andy's eye. In review, JSX's destinations page (read 23 September 2026) lists Dallas but not the airport; its Dallas page returned only an error. Love Field itself rests on Wikipedia (archived and current).
